findings.checklist_item: Add an acceptance criterion (or an [operator-attested] step) that confirms the three fixed skills actually register in a live Copilot CLI session (e.g. record the CLI's skill-list output on the ticket), or document why exercising the live CLI is deferred and note the residual risk that the inferred 1024/YAML constraints don't fully capture registration rules.
evidence: Context: 'silently fail to register in GitHub Copilot CLI'
The 1024 cap and YAML-strictness are asserted from 'github/copilot-cli#3494; YAML strictness in #1024', an external-system assumption
All five ACs verify frontmatter validity, not registration; no step loads skills into the live CLI
findings.finding: No acceptance criterion exercises the actual end-state — that Copilot CLI now registers the three previously-dropped skills. All ACs verify a proxy (YAML parses, description <=1024, trigger present) inferred from GitHub issues #3494/#1024, but none loads the fixed skills into the live Copilot CLI to confirm they register. The plan could pass every AC while the skills still silently fail to register if the CLI enforces an additional undocumented constraint.
scenarios: Skills pass the lint and CI is green, but Copilot CLI still drops one due to a constraint not captured by the lint (e.g. a name collision, a required field, or a stricter cap).

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Cite the source for the lint's `name` length (<=64) and regex constraints (Copilot CLI / Agent Skills spec ref), or mark them as UNVERIFIED and route to a quick spike to confirm against the spec/`--help` before wiring the gate into `make lint`.
evidence: Plan asserts the lint must check '`name` (when present) is <= 64 chars and matches `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`' with no citation, whereas the description cap is attributed to 'the Agent Skills spec's 1024-character description cap (github/copilot-cli#3494)'.
UNVERIFIED: the Copilot CLI name-validation surface could not be probed from the repo; recalled spec values must be treated as unverified.
Evidence class: Unverified (external `name` constraint surface unconfirmed).
findings.finding: The lint's `name` constraints (<= 64 chars and regex `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`) are asserted as the rule to enforce but are not grounded in any cited Copilot CLI / Agent Skills spec source, unlike the 1024-char description cap (which is at least attributed to github/copilot-cli#3494). If Copilot's actual `name` validation differs, the new gate codifies a fabricated external rule.
scenarios: A legitimately valid future skill name (e.g. exactly 64+ chars, or a name Copilot accepts but the regex rejects) fails the new gate — or an actually-invalid name passes because the enforced rule diverges from Copilot's real one.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a spec citation (issue/doc URL) for the name rule alongside the existing #3494 description-cap citation, or downgrade the name check to advisory (warn, non-failing) until the constraint is verified against Copilot's actual validator.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the 1024-char cap value and character-vs-byte / pre-vs-post-fold measurement semantics against Copilot CLI docs or a live skill-load test, and record the evidence class (Verified/Unverified) so the trim target is grounded rather than recalled from the cited issues.
evidence: Plan: 'Copilot CLI enforces the Agent Skills spec's 1024-character description cap ... but drops non-conforming skills silently ... (github/copilot-cli#3494; YAML strictness in #1024).'
The issue references are recalled/cited but not tool-confirmable from the repo; per T3 empiricism, recalled external limits are UNVERIFIED until observed.
Evidence class: Unverified (cap value and silent-drop behavior cited to issues, not observed).
findings.finding: The two central external behaviors the fix depends on — the exact 1024-char description cap and the 'silently drops non-conforming skills' parse behavior — are attributed to GitHub issues (#3494, #1024) but not verified against Copilot CLI docs/--help; no spike is proposed to confirm the cap value/behavior before committing the full fix (which trims descriptions precisely to <=1024).
scenarios: If the real cap is not exactly 1024 (or is measured differently, e.g. bytes vs chars, or applies post-fold vs pre-fold), a description trimmed to '<=1024' by the lint could still be dropped by Copilot at load time, and the fix would not actually re-register the skills.
